entries.definition: A person you know a little, but who is not a close friend.
entries.example: I said hello to an acquaintance from my old office.

entries.definition: A meeting of people who have not been together for a long time.
entries.example: Our school reunion was full of old stories.

entries.definition: The friendly way you welcome and look after guests.
entries.example: Their hospitality made me feel at home at once.

entries.definition: A movement of your hand, head, or body that shows a feeling or greeting.
entries.example: A bow is a common greeting gesture in Japan.

entries.definition: Polite behavior that shows respect for other people.
entries.example: She thanked the driver out of courtesy.

entries.definition: The feeling or opinion you form about someone when you first meet.
entries.example: His calm smile left a good impression.

entries.definition: To bend your head or upper body forward as a formal greeting.
entries.example: Visitors often bow when they meet the host.

entries.definition: The soft side of your face, sometimes touched in a greeting kiss.
entries.example: In that city, friends kiss each other on the cheek.

entries.definition: Able to speak a language easily and smoothly.
entries.example: She is fluent in English and Spanish.

entries.definition: A way of pronouncing words that shows where you are from.
entries.example: I like his soft southern accent.

entries.definition: The shared customs, ideas, and ways of living of a group of people.
entries.example: Greeting customs change from culture to culture.

entries.definition: A usual way of doing something in a particular place or group.
entries.example: It is the custom here to shake hands.

entries.definition: To move around a group and talk to different people.
entries.example: Try to mingle for ten minutes before you sit down.

entries.definition: Friendly and easy to start a conversation with.
entries.example: The new host is very approachable.

entries.definition: A question you ask when you have not seen someone for a while.
entries.example: How have you been since the summer course?

entries.definition: A polite way to start telling people who you are.
entries.example: Let me introduce myself. I am the new club leader.

entries.headword: I would like you to meet
entries.definition: Words you use when you present one person to another.
entries.example: I would like you to meet my classmate, Nora.

entries.definition: To continue to talk or write to someone after you part.
entries.example: Let's keep in touch after the semester ends.

entries.headword: it is a pleasure to meet you
entries.definition: A formal way to say you are glad to meet someone.
entries.example: It is a pleasure to meet you, Dr Singh.

entries.definition: To cause someone to think well of you at the start.
entries.example: Dress neatly if you want to make a good impression.

entries.definition: A friend that two people both know.
entries.example: We discovered we have a mutual friend in Seoul.

entries.definition: At the time when two people see each other for the first time.
entries.example: He seemed shy on first meeting, then relaxed.

entries.definition: A way that customs or values are not the same between groups.
entries.example: A greeting can show a cultural difference.

entries.definition: To say or do something that helps people relax at the start.
entries.example: The host told a short story to break the ice.

entries.definition: To help a person stop feeling nervous.
entries.example: A warm question can put someone at ease at a first meeting.

entries.definition: Friendly enough with someone to use first names.
entries.example: After one meeting we were already on first-name terms.
